source.title: From Knots to Knobs: Towards Steerable Collaborative Filtering Using Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Martin Spišák; Ladislav Peška; Petr Skoda; Vojtěch Vančura; Rodrigo Alves

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and table formatting are flattened, but the text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE-based interpretation and steering to collaborative-filtering autoencoders, a new model setting, and reports interpretability-related results. It does not test the specified language-model or vision-model claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures tag–neuron selectivity in collaborative-filtering models and tests recommendation steering. It does not report the fraction of neurons with one main job, test explanations on held-out activating examples, or evaluate simulated neuron explanations on new text. The reported selectivity metrics are proxies, not a direct audit of single-job neurons. Results on sparse-reconstruction accuracy in Section 4.2 do not measure the claim's interpretability behavior and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on collaborative-filtering autoencoder embeddings and measures tag selectivity and steering of SAE latents. It reports no audit of a model's own neurons, no language or vision model, no attribution graphs and no simulation scoring. SAE features are a trained replacement basis, not the network's neurons that the versions name. It therefore tests no version; the reader's 'tests/T3' is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE latents inserted in CFAEs are largely monosemantic, with many mapping to compact metadata concepts, and that steering via them is plausible. They also find TopK SAEs preserve accuracy for cosine-like embeddings and that not all CFAE architectures suit sparse reconstruction and steering.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK SAEs on collaborative-filtering user embeddings and maps neurons to item tags; it does not reproduce the cited language-model neuron-audit methods or estimate their one-job shares.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretability/selectivity varied by CFAE backbone and SAE reconstruction loss; steering differed by mapping strategy and backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latents on CFAE user embeddings show selective tag associations. 88%/59%/88% of tags have D_KL>10 for MultVAE+L2, ELSA+L2 and ELSA+Cosine; mean entropies are 6.3/8.3/9.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features trained on recommender embeddings align with item-metadata concepts, with selectivity depending on backbone and loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering via SAE latents works for ELSA+L2. It fails for MultVAE+L2 with representative-neuron mapping and is only partly remedied with unique neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-based steering of CF recommenders depends on backbone and concept-neuron mapping.

record.problems: Interpretability evidence is based on metadata-tag selectivity, not direct tests of whether each neuron has one job. The interpretability and steering experiments use ML-25M; the paper describes coarse segments and simple mapping methods, and notes architecture-dependent limitations. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the interpretability metrics or steering outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.3 also reports individual high- and low-KL tags in Table 2 and plots distributions in Figure 3. They are not itemized here because they are tag-level examples or figure distributions of the selectivity measures already recorded in R1–R6, not direct tests of single-job neuron shares. Section 4.2 reconstruction and downstream-accuracy results were omitted because they do not measure interpretability.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job shares.
No language models, dense or MoE, and no scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No test of architecture or tools raising the share of interpretable raw neurons.
No attribution graphs built from native neurons.
No check of explanations against held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: The 'monosemantic' claim concerns SAE dictionary features, not the network's own neurons, so it cannot bear on the essay's claim that raw neurons are already clean. Appendix B.2 gives qualitative examples of merged concepts (e.g., neuron id3125 for space tags), also SAE-level. All rows correctly keep versions none.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole counts, or proportions of one-job, two-job, or not-understood poles.
No language-model comparison or scaling study across dense/MoE models or parameter counts.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
No test of the stated architecture/tool explanation or estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
No test of explanations against held-out activating examples or prediction of where a neuron fires.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: MultVAE+L2
rows.operation_detail: Measured tag-to-neuron activation-distribution KL divergence; reported the share of entries above 10.
rows.measure: Share of tag-to-neuron entries with D_KL > 10
rows.note: Measures tag-specific selectivity, not the share of neurons with one main job.
rows.check: Tag-level KL selectivity of SAE latents in a recommender, not a share of model neurons with one job. Rows R2–R6 have the same problem.

rows.subject: ELSA+L2
rows.operation_detail: Steered recommendations toward the user's most distinctive held-out tag segment using the most-unique-neuron mapping.
rows.measure: Recommendation relevance and alignment toward target segment
rows.value: Recommendations became more aligned with the target segment, but covered only a fraction of it and had an inferior relevance-versus-steering tradeoff to the representative-neuron mapping.
rows.note: Steering result; it does not directly measure the fraction of single-job neurons.
rows.check: Steering-performance result for the study's own pipeline; no interpretability share. Rows R8–R10 have the same problem.

rows.subject: ELSA+L2
rows.operation_detail: Steered recommendations toward the user's most distinctive held-out tag segment using the most-representative-neuron mapping.
rows.measure: Recommendation relevance and alignment toward target segment
rows.value: Recommendations were relevant and more aligned toward the target segment; this mapping had a better relevance-versus-steering tradeoff than the most-unique-neuron mapping.
rows.note: Steering result; it does not directly measure the fraction of single-job neurons.

rows.subject: MultVAE+L2
rows.operation_detail: Steered recommendations toward the user's most distinctive held-out tag segment using the most-representative-neuron mapping.
rows.measure: Ability to produce recommendations steered toward target segment
rows.value: Boosting representative neurons completely failed to deliver steered recommendations; the authors attribute this to large overlaps in the mapping across tags.
rows.note: Steering result; it does not directly measure the fraction of single-job neurons.

rows.subject: MultVAE+L2
rows.operation_detail: Steered recommendations toward the user's most distinctive held-out tag segment using the most-unique-neuron mapping.
rows.measure: Ability to produce recommendations steered toward target segment and relevance tradeoff
rows.value: Using unique neurons partially remedied the failure, but results remained inferior to ELSA+L2.
rows.note: Steering result; it does not directly measure the fraction of single-job neurons.
